independentEvidence.conclusion: The URI is an entity identification scheme namespace (not required to be web-resolvable) used by DART contexts for the 8-digit DART corporation code.
independentEvidence.notSufficientAlone: That all 60 v1 files contained the URI motivated the follow-up but is not treated as evidence.
independentEvidence.provenance: Supplied by the requester in the task instructions before this freeze. The authoring environment's egress proxy blocks these hosts, so the sources were not re-fetched here; their content is recorded as cited, not independently re-verified by the author.

sources.establishes: The entity identifier element's required scheme attribute holds the namespace URI of the identification scheme; XBRL assumes no application can resolve the identifier or scheme URI.
sources.title: XBRL 2.1 Specification, XBRL International

sources.establishes: corp_code is the disclosing company's 8-digit corporation code (example 00126380).
sources.title: OpenDART developer guide (FSS)

sources.establishes: An XBRL context example shows <identifier scheme="http://dart.fss.or.kr/ifrs/CIK">00126380</identifier>, the same 8-digit value OpenDART gives as a corporation code.
sources.title: KPMG Korea XBRL seminar material, 2023-04-28

independentEvidence.whyNotBroader: The evidence names one URI. It says nothing about other paths, hosts, schemes or identifier types, and a scheme URI is an opaque namespace name, so prefix or wildcard matching would admit identifiers no evidence covers.
